title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

reading.body:
This is an access-control failure inside a law enforcement deployment, not a failure of the camera or database technology itself. The systems involved, a Flock camera network and the CJIS and CORI databases, are built to be queried by authorised personnel for legitimate police purposes. The alleged misuse happened at the point of use, where an officer with valid credentials is the only check between the system and the person being looked up.

Catching this kind of failure requires logging and review that treats each query as an auditable event tied to a case or reason, and a process that notices repeated searches for one individual with no investigative basis. The reporting does not establish what audit or oversight was in place at the Stow department, or whether any query review occurred before the woman raised the matter herself.

The accusation against Rogers is an allegation, and the criminal complaint and internal affairs investigation are not findings of guilt. What the reporting does not establish is his intent, the outcome of either process, or whether the searches were conducted on duty or with department equipment.

reports.title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

summary:
A Stow police officer, Jason Rogers, is accused of misusing police databases to track a woman he previously dated. The woman said she ended the abusive relationship about five years ago and changed her identity, phone number, and social media habits. She discovered this summer that Rogers had searched for her location using the Flock camera system and other law enforcement databases, including CJIS and CORI, multiple times in 2024 and 2025. She also said he drove by her home.

The Stow Police Department filed a criminal complaint against Rogers on July 17 and opened an internal affairs investigation. He was placed on paid leave in July, then unpaid leave as of July 31. The woman has obtained a restraining order lasting at least a year. A Select Board hearing is scheduled next week, when town leaders could vote on Rogers' employment status.
